chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Furat, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever wishes to be the wealthiest of people, let him rely more on what is in the Hand of Allah than on what is in the hands of others.'

key_terms.بِمَا فِي يَدِ غَيْرِهِ: What is in the hands of others
key_terms.يَدِ اللَّهِ: The Hand of Allah (symbolizing power and provision)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be the wealthiest person according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on Contentment, this hadith links material sufficiency to spiritual trust (tawakkun), teaching that true wealth lies in relying on God rather than people. It reflects the Shia emphasis on inner independence (ghina) achieved through divine reliance, distinguishing between transient worldly accumulation and enduring spiritual security.
